exposure: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) in women with movement disorders (Parkinson's disease, dystonia, Tourette's syndrome) or psychiatric diseases (Obsessive Compulsive Disorder)
outcome: maternal clinical status (motor and behavioral disorders)
cohort: The participants were women, followed in two DBS centers, who became pregnant and gave birth while suffering from disabling movement disorders or psychiatric diseases treated by Deep Brain Stimulation.
finding: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) is safe for young women with movement disorders, Tourette's syndrome, and Obsessive Compulsive Disorder to become pregnant and give birth, and it appears to improve their quality of life by enabling pregnancy and childbearing.
